title: The completion of a discrete valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local domain whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by a single nonzero element (a discrete valuation ring, Stacks Algebra Lemma Tag 00PD (4)), and let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ be its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by a single nonzero element; that is, $A^\wedge$ is again a discrete valuation ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr), direction 'A DVR implies A^ DVR'; its proof uses More on Algebra Lemmas lemma-completion-dimension and lemma-completion-regular and Algebra Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr)

proof.text: (Setup.) Write $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ for the canonical map and let $\pi\in A$ be a nonzero generator of $\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak m=\pi A$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] (with $I=\mathfrak m$), and it is a local ring whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, the ideal generated by $\iota(\mathfrak m)$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. As $\iota(\mathfrak m)=\iota(\pi)\iota(A)\subseteq\iota(\pi)A^\wedge$ and $\iota(\pi)\in\iota(\mathfrak m)$, this ideal is $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}=\mathfrak mA^\wedge=\iota(\pi)A^\wedge$, generated by the single element $\iota(\pi)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr), proof: "This follows from Lemmas 07NV and 07NY and Algebra, Lemma 00PD"; the completion is Noetherian local with maximal ideal mA^ as recalled in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NY

proof.text:
($\dim A=1$.) Since $A$ is a domain, $(0)$ is a prime ideal, and $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ because $\pi
eq0$; so $\dim A\ge1$. Conversely let $\mathfrak p
eq(0)$ be a prime ideal of $A$ and $0
eq x\in\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] (applied to $B=A$, whose hypothesis is exactly ours), $x=u\pi^n$ with $u\in A^	imes$, $n\ge0$; then $\pi^n=u^{-1}x\in\mathfrak p$, and $n\ge1$ because $\mathfrak p$ contains no unit, so $\pi\in\mathfrak p$ as $\mathfrak p$ is prime; hence $\mathfrak m=\pi A\subseteq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$ (every proper ideal of the local ring $A$ lies in $\mathfrak m$), i.e. $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$. So the prime ideals of $A$ are exactly $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ and $\dim A=1$.

proof.text: ($A$ is regular of dimension $1$.) $A$ is a Noetherian local ring with $\dim A=1$ (step 2) whose maximal ideal is generated by the $1=\dim A$ element $\pi$; by definition [def-weil-regular-scheme], $A$ is a regular local ring of dimension $1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), (4) implies (3); Definition Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local)

proof.text: ($A^\wedge$ is regular of dimension $1$.) Since $A$ is a regular local ring (step 3), so is $A^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] (direction $A$ regular $\Rightarrow$ $A^\wedge$ regular), and $\dim A^\wedge=\dim A=1$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr), proof: "This follows from Lemmas 07NV and 07NY and Algebra, Lemma 00PD"; Lemmas Tag 07NY (lemma-completion-regular) and Tag 07NV (lemma-completion-dimension)

proof.text: ($A^\wedge$ is a domain.) A regular local ring is a domain [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]; by step 4 this applies to $A^\wedge$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NP (lemma-regular-domain), as used in the proof of Lemma Tag 00PD, (3) implies (4): 'Note that a regular local ring is a domain'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $\iota(\pi)\neq0$: otherwise $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}=\iota(\pi)A^\wedge=0$ (step 1), so every prime ideal of the local ring $A^\wedge$, lying in $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}$, would be $0$ and $\dim A^\wedge=0$, contradicting $\dim A^\wedge=1$ (step 4). Hence $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian local ring (step 1), a domain (step 5), whose maximal ideal is generated by the single nonzero element $\iota(\pi)$ (step 1): a discrete valuation ring in the sense of Stacks 00PD (4).
